jobs.title: Global Public Policy Manager, Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI

reading.body:
Three open roles in AI policy and governance is too small a sample to support any claim about hiring trends.

The three postings do share a subject. One is a consultancy role in Munich, one is a reporting job, and one is a public policy manager position at Cohere covering compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI. Two of the three sit inside the policy function rather than the technical one, and only the Cohere listing names compute and infrastructure directly.

That Cohere title is the only place where the policy layer touches the physical layer. Sovereign AI and compute infrastructure are grid and datacenter questions before they are regulatory ones, so a policy hire framed around them is a small signal that the buildout now needs people who can argue about siting, power, and jurisdiction. One listing is not a pattern, and the other two roles could exist in any industry.

What the data does not cover matters more than what it does. There is no salary, no seniority distribution beyond the word senior in one title, no count of how many such roles went unfilled, and no history to compare against. The source list includes aggregators and company boards, but the three results here come from only two of them. Nothing in this data says whether policy hiring is rising, falling, or flat.
